finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-controlled params[:state] through Base64.decode64 into Marshal.load, enabling remote code execution as the service user.
finding.source: params[:state] on POST /restore (app.rb:5-6), no auth guard, no signature on the blob.

trace.note: post "/restore" route registered with no authentication or authorization guard.
params[:state] is base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load, which instantiates arbitrary Ruby objects and runs gadget chains during deserialization.
state.inspect runs only after deserialization has already occurred, so it does not mitigate the issue.

finding.guards_checked: No route auth guard; no HMAC/signature verification of the state blob; no class allowlist or switch to a safe format (JSON); no upstream sanitizing middleware defined in the codebase.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 registers post "/restore" with no before filter, auth helper, or middleware. app.rb:6 calls Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(params[:state])) with no signature check or class allowlist. The grep for before/helper/authenticate/use/Rack found no guards in the directory. app.rb:7 runs only after deserialization, so it does not mitigate.
verdict.reason: The route at app.rb:5 is anonymous and app.rb:6 passes attacker-supplied params[:state] straight into Marshal.load with no guard, so any remote caller reaches unsafe deserialization. Actual code execution depends on gadget classes loaded in the process, which this single file does not show, but Marshal.load on untrusted input is treated as RCE-equivalent.
